title: Your First Weekend at University of New Hampshire, Shared as Cards
description: A low-pressure first-weekend loop through central campus, its study and arts spaces, recreation, food, and nearby woods.

cards.title: Start at the MUB
cards.subtitle: Campus-life hub, Durham campus
cards.notes: Use the Memorial Union Building as your first indoor landmark: check the public activity listings, orient yourself, and choose a next stop together.
cards.short_summary: A central starting point for campus activities and services.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH identifies the Memorial Union Building as a place where Wildcats gather for events, activities, and everyday hangout.
cards.source_title: Durham Campus | University of New Hampshire
cards.access_notes: Building and departmental schedules vary; confirm access on the MUB site before visiting.

cards.title: Play a quick round in the Games Room
cards.subtitle: Room 154A, Memorial Union Building
cards.notes: Bring a new acquaintance to MUB room 154A for billiards, table tennis, or video games; ask staff about availability when you arrive.
cards.short_summary: A named MUB room for casual games.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH says the Games Room in MUB room 154A offers billiards, table tennis, and video games.
cards.source_title: Venues & Services | Memorial Union & Student Activities
cards.access_notes: Equipment and room availability may vary; check with the MUB during its open hours.

cards.title: Meet at the Wildcat Sculpture
cards.subtitle: Street side of Memorial Field
cards.notes: Make the bronze Wildcat Sculpture a simple outdoor photo-and-meetup point before continuing across campus; keep clear of any athletic activity nearby.
cards.short_summary: A documented bronze wildcat artwork beside Memorial Field.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Library documents that the bronze Wildcat Sculpture is on the street side of Memorial Field and was unveiled during 2006 Homecoming Weekend.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public artwork; observe it from pedestrian areas and follow posted event controls.

cards.title: Find your bearings at Dimond Library
cards.subtitle: 18 Library Way, Durham
cards.notes: Walk through the main Durham library, locate the information desk, and note a quiet floor or service you may want to use during the semester.
cards.short_summary: UNH’s main Durham library, with research collections and student-facing services.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH identifies Ezekiel W. Dimond Library as the main library on the Durham campus and lists its collections, Special Collections, and University Archives.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours before arrival; services and floor access can vary.

cards.title: See what is hanging at the UNH Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Paul Creative Arts Center
cards.notes: Drop into the UNH Art Gallery during regular business hours and look for the current exhibition; pair the visit with a walk around the arts center.
cards.short_summary: A free gallery in the Paul Creative Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH states that the UNH Art Gallery is in the Paul Creative Arts Center and has free admission during regular business hours.
cards.source_title: Latest on the UNH Art Gallery
cards.access_notes: Free during regular business hours; exhibitions and access may change, so confirm before going.

cards.title: Take a daylight walk in College Woods
cards.subtitle: West side of the main campus
cards.notes: Use the documented main entrance for a daytime walk, jog, or bird-watch; stay on suitable routes and bring layers for changing New Hampshire weather.
cards.short_summary: A 250-acre university woodland used for recreation and teaching.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH describes College Woods as about 250 acres on the west side of main campus, with hiking, walking, skiing, jogging, bird watching, and relaxation among its recreational uses.
cards.source_title: College Woods | UNH College of Life Sciences and Agriculture
cards.access_notes: Use the official directions and visit in daylight; hiking and biking have different allowed areas.

cards.title: Scope out Hamel Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 5 Edgewood Road, Durham
cards.notes: Visit the Hamel Recreation Center welcome area to learn how campus recreation access works and choose a future class, facility, or outdoor activity.
cards.short_summary: The campus recreation entry point for student membership and facility access.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH’s Campus Recreation student membership page lists Hamel Recreation Center among fall and spring membership benefits for eligible students.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Student Membership | UNH Campus Recreation
cards.access_notes: Ask the welcome center about eligibility and current facility schedules; access depends on membership or enrollment status.

cards.title: Plan a warm-weather pool visit
cards.subtitle: Accessed through Hamel Recreation Center
cards.notes: If it is in season, review the pool schedule first, then bring swim gear for a relaxed lap or free-swim session with friends.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal UNH pool with lap lanes and free-swim space.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH describes the Outdoor Pool as having zero-depth entry, swim lanes, and space for free swimming, with entrance through Hamel Recreation Center.
cards.access_notes: Season is late June through early September, weather permitting; check the current facility calendar and access eligibility.

cards.title: Have a meal at Holloway Commons
cards.subtitle: Central campus dining hall
cards.notes: Use a meal swipe or pay at the counter for a first shared campus meal; review the live menu and allergen information before choosing a station.
cards.short_summary: UNH’s centrally located largest dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH identifies Holloway Commons as its largest, centrally located dining hall and states that students can enter dining halls with fingerprint ID or by paying at the counter.
cards.source_title: Admitted Students Guide: Campus Dining | Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Meal swipe or payment is required; current menus and schedules may change for holidays and events.

cards.title: Check the Dairy Bar’s seasonal opening
cards.subtitle: 3 Depot Road, Durham
cards.notes: When it is open, stop at the Dairy Bar for food or ice cream and take note of its historic train-station setting near the Durham depot.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal UNH dining location in a historic train-station building.
cards.evidence_claim: UNH Dining lists the Dairy Bar at 3 Depot Road and notes that its hours can change; UNH Archives documents that it is housed in the historic train station.
cards.access_notes: Currently seasonal; verify current opening dates and hours on UNH Dining before making the walk.
